references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 23:4|Matthew 23:4] where Jesus says that the scribes and Pharisees tie up heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to move them with a finger.
Later in the same speech, in [ref:Luk 11:52|Luke 11:52], Jesus expands his criticism of the experts in the law: they have taken away the key of knowledge and prevent others from entering.

In [ref:Apg 15:10|Acts 15:10] Peter speaks about putting a yoke on the disciples' necks that neither their ancestors nor they themselves were able to bear—a direct parallel to the heavy burdens imposed on the people by the experts in the law.
In [ref:Apg 15:28|Acts 15:28] the apostles and elders decide not to place any other burden on believers than what is necessary, in contrast to the practice of the experts in the law.
In [ref:Matt 23:2-4|Matthew 23:2-4] Jesus describes the hypocrisy of the Pharisees: they sit on Moses' seat and impose much on others, but do not do themselves what they require of others.

In [ref:Matt 11:28-30|Matthew 11:28-30] Jesus invites all who are weary and carrying heavy burdens to come to him, for his yoke is good and his burden is light—a strong contrast to the heavy burdens the experts in the law placed on people.
In [ref:Gal 6:13|Galatians 6:13] Paul points out that those who demand circumcision do not even keep the law—the same pattern of hypocrisy that Jesus criticizes in the experts in the law.

In [ref:Jes 10:1|Isaiah 10:1] a woe is pronounced against those who enact unjust laws and write oppressive decrees, similar to Jesus' woes against the experts in the law who laid heavy burdens on the people.

In [ref:Gal 6:2|Galatians 6:2] Paul encourages believers to bear one another's burdens and thus fulfill Christ's law—a positive contrast to the experts in the law who placed burdens on others without helping.
In [ref:Rom 2:21-23|Romans 2:21-23] Paul questions those who teach others but do not follow their own teaching—the same hypocrisy Jesus accuses the experts in the law of.
